# Foreman Executor connection

Foreman runs on Executor v2 with three lanes, each a v2 member user (a bot) in its own v2 group: `foreman-root`, `foreman-support` and `foreman-disputes`. Each app is shared only with the groups of the lanes that use it. Every lane calls the plain `<EXECUTOR_BASE_URL>/mcp` with its own bot's personal access token, so a lane reaches exactly the apps shared with its bot. Root, native delegates, critic, schedules, and authored provider helpers use the `foreman` lane. Ordinary workflows reuse it. ENG-13601 is a narrow exception: the explicitly stamped Intercom support schedules use `foreman-support`, including helpers and delegated reads, with journaled Linear writes. See [INTERCOM-SUPPORT-CRON.md](./INTERCOM-SUPPORT-CRON.md) for the existing-access audit, candidate policy and activation gates. ENG-16255 is the second deliberate exception: the Stripe dispute evidence update and evidence file upload live only in `foreman-disputes` (`.github/executor/disputes-toolkit-manifest.json`), on their own `foreman_stripe_dispute_write` app (and `foreman_stripe_dispute_write_sandbox` for Preview), and only `respond_stripe_dispute` reaches them through `invokeProvider`. The raw `execute` gateway runs any path in the shared toolkit and its approval cannot filter per operation, so a dispute write there would bypass the tool's human-approval gate for submit. Both dispute-write apps are shared only with the disputes bot's group (verified live: the root and support bot tokens get 403 on them), and only `invokeProvider` for a dispute-write path asks for the disputes connector, which only `respond_stripe_dispute` does. The shared manifest must never select a dispute write or file upload path (`agent/lib/executor.test.ts` and `agent/lib/executor/lane-auth.test.ts` check this). The dispute, charge, customer, and AI Acquisition Slack reads stay in the shared toolkit.

## What controls behavior

Skills and agent instructions define the workflow. Critic instructions require read-only review even though it shares the same connection. Linear writes and OpenRouter requests are available. Vercel REST operations use the `foreman_vercel_api` app with the owner-approved Foreman-scoped credential; billing charges use a separate `foreman_vercel_billing_api` app on the team-scoped credential approved for that one operation, because v2 calls cannot choose between two accounts of one app. The manifest selects 352 REST operations. The 65 destructive operations recorded under `connectionPolicies` carry an `always` approval rule in the Foreman-only `foreman-vercel-api` and `foreman-vercel-billing-api` apps, and a lane bot cannot answer an approval, so no Foreman lane can run them. Hosted-MCP-only toolbar actions are not part of this REST connection. Resend retains the selected read operations. Provider credentials and their existing scopes stay in Executor. Autumn includes all 18 read-only API operations and all 20 MCP reads, date utilities, and non-mutating previews in the installed catalog. Customer, subscription, balance, plan, catalog, and organization-rule mutations remain excluded from the read-only Autumn surface.

The [tool availability audit](./EXECUTOR-TOOL-AVAILABILITY.md) lists restored reads and every remaining provider-tool exclusion.

The single operation list in `.github/executor/toolkit-manifest.json` records the selected company operations and known missing coverage. Residual risk: a bot token reaches every tool of every app shared with its group. v1 toolkits picked individual tools; v2 sharing is per app, so the manifests no longer enforce a tool list at Executor. Per-tool narrowing now lives in Foreman's own allowlists (support and widget catalogs and policies, the lane gates in `dispatch.ts`) and in each app's approval rules. The root lane's raw `execute` gateway can call any tool of the root lane's apps; the 65 destructive Vercel operations are the exception, because their `always` approval rule stops every bot call (see above). A tool path is `<app slug>.<tool>`, and the app slug is the app name with every run of other characters than `a-z0-9` replaced by `-` (`foreman_vercel_api` becomes `foreman-vercel-api`). Executor administration remains excluded. It does not divide permissions by workflow, requester, or subagent. Foreman's connection allows only `execute` and `skills`; it does not use approval resume. Personal Supermemory stays on its existing personal connection and sign-in path.

## Helpers and mappings

Authored helpers retain their public names, validation, fixed routes, pagination, workspace membership checks, field filtering, deadlines, and result formats. Their underlying API operations are included in the same toolkit and can be discovered directly. Helper use is instructed rather than enforced by a separate hidden catalog.

`.github/executor/operation-bindings.json` maps each helper operation to its installed tool path. Deployment configuration supplies paths only; validated typed arguments are owned by `agent/lib/executor/operations.ts` and the domain helpers. Typed helper schemas in `agent/lib/executor/operations.ts` group each OpenAPI input into v2's `{ path, query, headers, body }`; MCP inputs stay flat. The transport passes canonical inputs unchanged, so generic describe/call uses the installed schema directly. The client sends no URL reconstruction, HTTP-response fabrication, regex dispatch, or deployment coercions. The API definitions under `.github/executor/specs/` describe the custom connections.

Linear documents live in `agent/lib/linear-operations.ts`. `pnpm executor:specs` generates the read/write OpenAPI specs from those definitions; `pnpm validate` checks for generated-file drift. Query edits also require installing the updated spec in Executor before deploying the consuming Foreman revision.

v2 tools return the provider's data and throw on failure. The transport's program rebuilds the `{ ok, data }` / `{ ok: false, error: { code, status } }` outcome the typed client branches on, and reads the result from `execution.value`. v2 keeps no response headers, so a success status other than 200 and `Retry-After` no longer reach Foreman; the `error.retryAfter` path stays. Instantly honors short retry intervals, returns long intervals without sleeping, and does not retry a 429 without a usable interval. A tool whose app has a linked account takes `{ accountId, input }`; the program reads the account from `tools.search.describe` and wraps the helper's input, sends input unchanged when the tool has no account, refuses more than one account (`executor_account_ambiguous`), and lets input already shaped as `{ accountId, input }` through only for that same account (`executor_account_mismatch` otherwise), so caller input never chooses the account.

Each lane authenticates through its own app-scoped Vercel Connect API-key connector holding that lane's bot token: `EXECUTOR_MCP_CONNECTOR_FOREMAN`, `EXECUTOR_MCP_CONNECTOR_SUPPORT` (the widget lane reuses it) and `EXECUTOR_MCP_CONNECTOR_DISPUTES`. Every token request names its lane (`executorAuth(lane)` in `agent/lib/executor/auth.ts`); a missing lane connector fails as `executor_not_configured`, never falling back to another lane's connector. Tokens stay out of tool arguments and results. The transport uses a fresh MCP session per invocation, rejects redirects, bounds responses to 8 MiB, and composes its 50-second deadline with caller cancellation. Helper-specific bounds remain in place. There is no direct-provider fallback.

## Configuration and verification

- Set `EXECUTOR_OPERATION_BINDINGS` to the compact JSON contents of `.github/executor/operation-bindings.json` after verifying the installed catalog; the empty `.env.example` placeholder is not runnable provider configuration.
- `EXECUTOR_BASE_URL` defaults to `https://executor.acquisity.ai` and must be an HTTPS origin. Every lane uses `<EXECUTOR_BASE_URL>/mcp`; v2 ignores `?connection=` for tokens, so Foreman does not use scoped connections.
- `EXECUTOR_API_TOKEN` and the `EXECUTOR_LANE_TOKEN_*` values are for the operator readiness checks only and must never be set on a deployment: a personal access token keeps its owner's full access at every URL.
- `LINEAR_CONNECTOR` remains for inbound Agent Sessions and Linear attachment downloads. Slack delivery, GitHub, Blob, investigation memory, models, and sandbox infrastructure remain separate.
- `pnpm executor:contract` reports the endpoint, selected operations, and required helper mappings. `pnpm executor:readiness` checks ordinary coverage. Add `--live` with `EXECUTOR_API_TOKEN` (a v2 personal access token) and `EXECUTOR_ORGANIZATION` (organization ID or slug) to check that every manifest path names an installed app and tool, through `GET /api/organizations/<org>/inventory` and `/apps/<app>/tools`; add `--support` or `--widget` for those manifests. Add `--isolation` with `EXECUTOR_LANE_TOKEN_FOREMAN`, `_SUPPORT` and `_DISPUTES` (the bots' tokens) to check that each bot's inventory holds exactly its manifest's apps, the dispute-write apps only for disputes. The command never resolves provider credentials or invokes tools.
- Run `pnpm validate`, inspect compiled root/critic connections, and exercise platform reads, helper parity, expected writes on synthetic records, and critic read-only behavior on preview. Direct delivery evaluations require a scratch repository and an existing test ticket.
- Logs record only outer tool/connection names, outcome, and session/turn identifiers. Use Executor invocation records for provider diagnosis; never log tool arguments, results, credentials, or provider error bodies.

Preview evidence and remaining release gates are in `EXECUTOR-PREVIEW.md`. Production connector attachment and deployment still require the release procedure. Roll back by reverting on `main` and restoring the v1 environment values; v1 stays unchanged until the v2 cutover is accepted.

The root lane reaches Neon only through the Foreman-only `neon-readonly` app on `https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp?readonly=true`, never the shared `neon` app, so `neon-readonly.run_sql` and `neon-readonly.run_sql_transaction` run in read-only transactions. Keep that endpoint and the read-only MCP OAuth grant. On reconnect, leave Full access unchecked; do not add the `write` scope. The selected SQL tools depend on Neon enforcing read-only transactions. Resource mutations remain outside the exact Neon allowlist and are denied by default. This restriction does not change the separate direct investigation-memory connection.

For every PR, follow [EXECUTOR-PREVIEW.md](./EXECUTOR-PREVIEW.md): move the Foreman Preview Slack trigger to that PR branch, remove the previous Preview trigger branch, attach the actual Preview Executor connector and verified bindings, and redeploy before testing. Keep the Preview support database and queue separate from Production. Environment changes are not verified until the active deployment runs a real provider read.
